This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# 7-Zip

7-Zip is a file archiver with a high compression ratio.

## About

7-Zip is free software that provides:
- High compression ratio using the LZMA and LZMA2 compression algorithms
- Support for multiple archive formats (7z, ZIP, GZIP, BZIP2, TAR, and others)
- Strong AES-256 encryption in 7z and ZIP formats
- Self-extracting capability for 7z format
- Integration with Windows Shell
- Powerful command-line interface
- Plugin support for file managers

## Website

Official website: [7-zip.org](https://7-zip.org)

## License

7-Zip is distributed under the GNU LGPL license (with some components under other open-source licenses).
See the DOC directory for detailed license information.

## Supported Formats

**Packing / unpacking**: 7z, XZ, BZIP2, GZIP, TAR, ZIP and WIM

**Unpacking only**: APFS, AR, ARJ, CAB, CHM, CPIO, CramFS, DMG, EXT, FAT, GPT, HFS, IHEX, ISO, LZH, LZMA, MBR, MSI, NSIS, NTFS, QCOW2, RAR, RPM, SquashFS, UDF, UEFI, VDI, VHD, VHDX, VMDK, XAR and Z.

Read "License.txt" for more infomation about license.

Notes about unRAR license:

Please check main restriction from unRar license:

   2. The unRAR sources may be used in any software to handle RAR
      archives without limitations free of charge, but cannot be used
      to re-create the RAR compression algorithm, which is proprietary.
      Distribution of modified unRAR sources in separate form or as a

      stated in the documentation and source comments that the code may
      not be used to develop a RAR (WinRAR) compatible archiver.

In brief it means:
1) You can compile and use compiled files under GNU LGPL rules, since
   unRAR license almost has no restrictions for compiled files.
   You can link these compiled files to LGPL programs.
2) You can fix bugs in source code and use compiled fixed version.
3) You can not use unRAR sources to re-create the RAR compression algorithm.


LZMA SDK
--------

This package also contains some files from LZMA SDK
You can download LZMA SDK from:
  http://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html
LZMA SDK is written and placed in the public domain by Igor Pavlov.


How to compile in Windows
-------------------------

To compile the sources to Windows binaries you need Visual Studio compiler and/or Windows SDK.
You can use latest Windows Studio 2017/2019/2022 to compile binaries for x86, x64, arm64 and arm platforms.
Also you can use old compilers for some platforms:
  x86   : Visual C++ 6.0 with Platform SDK
  x64   : Windows Server 2003 R2 Platform SDK
  ia64 (itanium)  : Windows Server 2003 R2 Platform SDK
  arm for Windows CE : Standard SDK for Windows CE 5.0

If you use MSVC6, specify also Platform SDK directories at top of directories lists:
Tools / Options / Directories
  - Include files
  - Library files

Also you need Microsoft Macro Assembler:
  - ml.exe for x86
  - ml64.exe for x64
You can use ml.exe from Windows SDK for Windows Vista or some later versions.

There are two ways to compile 7-Zip binaries:
1) via makefile in command line.
2) via dsp file in Visual Studio.

The dsp file compiling can be used for development and debug purposes.
All final 7-Zip binaries are compiled via makefiles, that provide best
optimization options.


How to compile with makefile in Windows
---------------------------------------

Some macronames can be defined for compiling with makefile:

PLATFORM
  with possible values: x64, x86, arm64, arm, ia64

OLD_COMPILER
  for old VC compiler, like MSCV 6.0.

MY_DYNAMIC_LINK
  for dynamic linking to the run-time library (msvcrt.dll).
  The default makefile option is static linking to the run-time library.

To compile all 7-Zip files for x64 with Visual Studio 2022,
use the following command sequence:

  cd SRC\CPP\7zip
  %comspec% /k "C:\Program Files\VS2022\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"
  nmake

You can use another "vcvars*.bat" files from "VS2022\VC\Auxiliary\Build" directory
to compile for other platforms:
  vcvars64.bat
  vcvarsamd64_arm64.bat
  vcvarsamd64_x86.bat

Also you can compile single binary from directory with related project.
For example, to compile 7za.exe, use the following command sequence:
  cd SRC\CPP\7zip\Bundles\Alone\
  nmake


Compiling 7-Zip for Unix/Linux
------------------------------

There are several options to compile 7-Zip with different compilers: gcc and clang.
Also 7-Zip code contains two versions for some parts of code: in C and in Assembeler.
So if you compile the version with Assembeler code, you will get faster 7-Zip binary.

7-Zip's assembler code uses the following syntax for different platforms:

1) x86 and x86-64 (AMD64): MASM syntax.
   Now there are 3 programs that supports MASM syntax in Linux.
'    'Asmc Macro Assembler, JWasm, and UASM. Note that JWasm now doesn't support some
      cpu instructions used in 7-Zip.
   So you must install Asmc Macro Assembler in Linux or UASM, if you want to compile
   fastest version of 7-Zip  x86 and x86-64:
     https://github.com/nidud/asmc
     https://github.com/Terraspace/UASM


2) arm64: GNU assembler for ARM64 with preprocessor.
   That systax is supported by GCC and CLANG for ARM64.

There are different binaries that can be compiled from 7-Zip source.
There are 2 main files in folder for compiling:
  makefile        - that can be used for compiling Windows version of 7-Zip with nmake command
  makefile.gcc    - that can be used for compiling Linux/macOS versions of 7-Zip or Windows version
                    with MINGW (GCC) with make command.
                   
At first you must change the current folder to folder that contains `makefile.gcc`:

  cd CPP/7zip/Bundles/Alone2

    e_phoff = struct.unpack("<Q", data[0x20:0x28])[0]
    e_shoff = struct.unpack("<Q", data[0x28:0x30])[0]
    e_flags = struct.unpack("<I", data[0x30:0x34])[0]
    e_ehsize = struct.unpack("<H", data[0x34:0x36])[0]
    e_phentsize = struct.unpack("<H", data[0x36:0x38])[0]
    e_phnum = struct.unpack("<H", data[0x38:0x3A])[0]
    e_shentsize = struct.unpack("<H", data[0x3A:0x3C])[0]
    e_shnum = struct.unpack("<H", data[0x3C:0x3E])[0]
    e_shstrndx = struct.unpack("<H", data[0x3E:0x40])[0]
    print(f"e_phoff {hex(e_phoff)} e_shoff {hex(e_shoff)} e_flags {hex(e_flags)} e_ehsize {e_ehsize} e_phentsize {e_phentsize} e_phnum {e_phnum} e_shentsize {e_shentsize} e_shnum {e_shnum}")
    for i in range(e_phnum):
        off = e_phoff + i*e_phentsize
        p_type, p_flags, p_offset, p_vaddr, p_paddr, p_filesz, p_memsz, p_align = struct.unpack("<IIQQQQQQ", data[off:off+56])

    print("max_end filesz", hex(max_end), max_end)
    # Section headers
    for i in range(min(e_shnum, 5)):
        off = e_shoff + i*e_shentsize
        s = struct.unpack("<IIQQQQIIQQ", data[off:off+64])
        print(f"SH {i}:", [hex(x) for x in s])

# 7-Zip

7-Zip is a file archiver with a high compression ratio.

## About

7-Zip is free software that provides:
- High compression ratio using the LZMA and LZMA2 compression algorithms
- Support for multiple archive formats (7z, ZIP, GZIP, BZIP2, TAR, and others)
- Strong AES-256 encryption in 7z and ZIP formats
- Self-extracting capability for 7z format
- Integration with Windows Shell
- Powerful command-line interface
- Plugin support for file managers

## Website

Official website: [7-zip.org](https://7-zip.org)

## License

7-Zip is distributed under the GNU LGPL license (with some components under other open-source licenses).
See the DOC directory for detailed license information.

## Supported Formats

**Packing / unpacking**: 7z, XZ, BZIP2, GZIP, TAR, ZIP and WIM

**Unpacking only**: APFS, AR, ARJ, CAB, CHM, CPIO, CramFS, DMG, EXT, FAT, GPT, HFS, IHEX, ISO, LZH, LZMA, MBR, MSI, NSIS, NTFS, QCOW2, RAR, RPM, SquashFS, UDF, UEFI, VDI, VHD, VHDX, VMDK, XAR and Z.

For more information, visit the official 7-Zip website.

-------------------

7-Zip is a file archiver for Windows.

7-Zip Copyright (C) 1999-2026 Igor Pavlov.


License Info
------------

7-Zip is free software distributed under the GNU LGPL
(except for unRar code). Also some  code
is licensed under the "BSD 3-clause License".
Read "License.txt" for more infomation about license.

Notes about unRAR license:

Please check main restriction from unRar license:

   2. The unRAR sources may be used in any software to handle RAR
      archives without limitations free of charge, but cannot be used
      to re-create the RAR compression algorithm, which is proprietary.
      Distribution of modified unRAR sources in separate form or as a
      part of other software is permitted, provided that it is clearly
      stated in the documentation and source comments that the code may
      not be used to develop a RAR (WinRAR) compatible archiver.

In brief it means:
1) You can compile and use compiled files under GNU LGPL rules, since
   unRAR license almost has no restrictions for compiled files.
   You can link these compiled files to LGPL programs.
2) You can fix bugs in source code and use compiled fixed version.
3) You can not use unRAR sources to re-create the RAR compression algorithm.


LZMA SDK
--------

This package also contains some files from LZMA SDK
You can download LZMA SDK from:
  http://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html
LZMA SDK is written and placed in the public domain by Igor Pavlov.


How to compile in Windows
-------------------------

To compile the sources to Windows binaries you need Visual Studio compiler and/or Windows SDK.
You can use latest Windows Studio 2017/2019/2022 to compile binaries for x86, x64, arm64 and arm platforms.
Also you can use old compilers for some platforms:
  x86   : Visual C++ 6.0 with Platform SDK
  x64   : Windows Server 2003 R2 Platform SDK
  ia64 (itanium)  : Windows Server 2003 R2 Platform SDK
  arm for Windows CE : Standard SDK for Windows CE 5.0

If you use MSVC6, specify also Platform SDK directories at top of directories lists:
Tools / Options / Directories
  - Include files
  - Library files

Also you need Microsoft Macro Assembler:
  - ml.exe for x86
  - ml64.exe for x64
You can use ml.exe from Windows SDK for Windows Vista or some later versions.

There are two ways to compile 7-Zip binaries:
1) via makefile in command line.
2) via dsp file in Visual Studio.

The dsp file compiling can be used for development and debug purposes.
All final 7-Zip binaries are compiled via makefiles, that provide best
optimization options.


How to compile with makefile in Windows
---------------------------------------

Some macronames can be defined for compiling with makefile:

PLATFORM
  with possible values: x64, x86, arm64, arm, ia64

OLD_COMPILER
  for old VC compiler, like MSCV 6.0.

MY_DYNAMIC_LINK
  for dynamic linking to the run-time library (msvcrt.dll).
  The default makefile option is static linking to the run-time library.

To compile all 7-Zip files for x64 with Visual Studio 2022,
use the following command sequence:

  cd SRC\CPP\7zip
  %comspec% /k "C:\Program Files\VS2022\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"
  nmake

You can use another "vcvars*.bat" files from "VS2022\VC\Auxiliary\Build" directory
to compile for other platforms:
  vcvars64.bat

# 7-Zip

7-Zip is a file archiver with a high compression ratio.

## About

7-Zip is free software that provides:
- High compression ratio using the LZMA and LZMA2 compression algorithms
- Support for multiple archive formats (7z, ZIP, GZIP, BZIP2, TAR, and others)
- Strong AES-256 encryption in 7z and ZIP formats
- Self-extracting capability for 7z format
- Integration with Windows Shell
- Powerful command-line interface
- Plugin support for file managers

## Website

Official website: [7-zip.org](https://7-zip.org)

## License

7-Zip is distributed under the GNU LGPL license (with some components under other open-source licenses).
See the DOC directory for detailed license information.

## Supported Formats

**Packing / unpacking**: 7z, XZ, BZIP2, GZIP, TAR, ZIP and WIM

**Unpacking only**: APFS, AR, ARJ, CAB, CHM, CPIO, CramFS, DMG, EXT, FAT, GPT, HFS, IHEX, ISO, LZH, LZMA, MBR, MSI, NSIS, NTFS, QCOW2, RAR, RPM, SquashFS, UDF, UEFI, VDI, VHD, VHDX, VMDK, XAR and Z.

def crc64_ecma(data):
    # ECMA reflected with poly 0xC96C5795D7870F42, init 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, xorout same
    poly = 0xC96C5795D7870F42
    crc = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            if crc & 1:
                crc = (crc >> 1) ^ poly
            else:
                crc >>= 1
            crc &= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return crc ^ 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

def detect_type(path, override=None):
    if override:
        # Normalize override
        ov = override.lower()
        # Map
        if ov in ("7z","zip","tar","gzip","gz","bzip2","bz2","xz"):
            # Map gz->gzip, bz2->bzip2
            if ov == "gz":
                return "gzip"
            if ov == "bz2":
                return "bzip2"
            return ov
        else:
            return ov
    # Detect by extension
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    if ext == ".7z":
        return "7z"
    elif ext == ".zip":
        return "zip"
    elif ext == ".tar":
        return "tar"
    elif ext == ".gz" or ext == ".tgz":
        return "gzip"
    elif ext == ".bz2":
        return "bzip2"
    elif ext == ".xz":
        return "xz"
    elif ext == ".001":
        return "Split"
    else:
        # Try to detect by magic
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                magic = f.read(10)
                if magic.startswith(b"7z\xBC\xAF\x27\x1C"):
                    return "7z"
                elif magic.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04"):
                    return "zip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\x1F\x8B"):
                    return "gzip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"BZh"):
                    return "bzip2"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\xFD7zXZ\x00"):
                    return "xz"
                elif magic[257:262] == b"ustar":
                    return "tar"
        except:
            pass
        return "7z"

def crc64_ecma(data):
    # ECMA reflected with poly 0xC96C5795D7870F42, init 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, xorout same
    poly = 0xC96C5795D7870F42
    crc = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            if crc & 1:
                crc = (crc >> 1) ^ poly
            else:
                crc >>= 1
            crc &= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return crc ^ 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

def detect_type(path, override=None):
    if override:
        # Normalize override
        ov = override.lower()
        # Map
        if ov in ("7z","zip","tar","gzip","gz","bzip2","bz2","xz"):
            # Map gz->gzip, bz2->bzip2
            if ov == "gz":
                return "gzip"
            if ov == "bz2":
                return "bzip2"
            return ov
        else:
            return ov
    # Detect by extension
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    if ext == ".7z":
        return "7z"
    elif ext == ".zip":
        return "zip"
    elif ext == ".tar":
        return "tar"
    elif ext == ".gz" or ext == ".tgz":
        return "gzip"
    elif ext == ".bz2":
        return "bzip2"
    elif ext == ".xz":
        return "xz"
    elif ext == ".001":
        return "Split"
    else:
        # Try to detect by magic
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                magic = f.read(10)
                if magic.startswith(b"7z\xBC\xAF\x27\x1C"):
                    return "7z"
                elif magic.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04"):
                    return "zip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\x1F\x8B"):
                    return "gzip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"BZh"):
                    return "bzip2"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\xFD7zXZ\x00"):
                    return "xz"
                elif magic[257:262] == b"ustar":
                    return "tar"
        except:
            pass
        return "7z"

def crc64_ecma(data):
    poly = 0xC96C5795D7870F42
    crc = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            if crc & 1:
                crc = (crc >> 1) ^ poly
            else:
                crc >>= 1
            crc &= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return crc ^ 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

def detect_type(path, override=None):
    if override:
        ov = override.lower()
        if ov == "gz":
            return "gzip"
        if ov == "bz2":
            return "bzip2"
        if ov in ("7z","zip","tar","gzip","bzip2","xz"):
            return ov
        return ov
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    if ext == ".7z":
        return "7z"
    elif ext == ".zip":
        return "zip"
    elif ext == ".tar":
        return "tar"
    elif ext in (".gz",".tgz"):
        return "gzip"
    elif ext == ".bz2":
        return "bzip2"
    elif ext == ".xz":
        return "xz"
    elif ext == ".001":
        return "Split"
    else:
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                magic = f.read(10)
                if magic.startswith(b"7z\xBC\xAF\x27\x1C"):
                    return "7z"
                elif magic.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04"):
                    return "zip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\x1F\x8B"):
                    return "gzip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"BZh"):
                    return "bzip2"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\xFD7zXZ\x00"):
                    return "xz"
                elif len(magic) >= 262 and magic[257:262] == b"ustar":
                    return "tar"
        except:
            pass
        return "7z"

def handle_list(archive, archive_type, slt, password, bso):
    # bso handling
    if bso == "0":
        # No header at all? But for l -bso0, header suppressed
        header = ""
    elif bso == "2":
        sys.stderr.write(get_header())
        header = ""
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(get_header())
        header = ""
    # Check existence
    if not os.path.exists(archive):
        # Need to print scanning line
        out = sys.stdout if bso != "2" else sys.stderr
        cur = sys.stdout if bso != "0" else None
        # Actually scanning goes to same as header? For bso0, scanning suppressed?
        # For error case, scanning was always in stdout (except bso2 where it goes to stderr)
        # Let's handle simply: scanning to stdout unless bso2 then to stderr, and suppressed for bso0
        if bso == "0":
            pass
        elif bso == "2":
            sys.stderr.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
        else:
            sys.stdout.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
        # For bso0, we still need to not print scanning
        # Then error to stderr
        sys.stderr.write(f"\nERROR: errno=2 : No such file or directory\n{archive}\n\n\n\nSystem ERROR:\nerrno=2 : No such file or directory\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    # Detect type
    detected = detect_type(archive, archive_type)
    # If archive_type provided and mismatch, error
    actual = detect_type(archive, None)
    if archive_type and actual != detected:
        # Actually detected is override, actual is real. If override != actual, then error
        # But detect_type with override returns override, so we need actual
        # Let's get actual via detect_type without override
        real = detect_type(archive, None)
        if real != archive_type:
            # Print scanning
            if bso == "0":
                pass
            elif bso == "2":
                sys.stderr.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
                # Need size
                try:
                    sz = os.path.getsize(archive)
                    sys.stderr.write(f"1 file, {sz} bytes (1 KiB)\n\n")
                except:
                    sys.stderr.write("1 file, 0 bytes (0 KiB)\n\n")
                sys.stderr.write(f"Listing archive: {archive}\n\n")
            else:
                sys.stdout.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
                try:
                    sz = os.path.getsize(archive)
                    sys.stdout.write(f"1 file, {sz} bytes (1 KiB)\n\n")
                except:
                    sys.stdout.write("1 file, 0 bytes (0 KiB)\n\n")
                sys.stdout.write(f"Listing archive: {archive}\n\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {archive} : {archive}\nOpen ERROR: Cannot open the file as [{archive_type}] archive\n\n\nERRORS:\nIs not archive\n\n")
            sys.exit(2)
    # Now normal list
    # For bso handling, scanning and listing streams
    # For bso0: header suppressed, but scanning also suppressed, listing still in stdout
    # For bso1: header in stdout, scanning in stdout, listing in stdout
    # For bso2: header in stderr, scanning in stderr, listing in stdout
    # So we need to handle
    if bso == "0":
        # No header, no scanning header? But we already handled header. Now we need to print scanning? For bso0, scanning not printed
        # So skip scanning
        pass
    elif bso == "2":
        sys.stderr.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
        try:
            sz = os.path.getsize(archive)
            sys.stderr.write(f"1 file, {sz} bytes (1 KiB)\n\n")
        except:
            sys.stderr.write("1 file, 0 bytes (0 KiB)\n\n")
        # Listing archive line goes to stdout? Actually for bso2, listing was in stdout
        sys.stdout.write(f"Listing archive: {archive}\n\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
        try:
            sz = os.path.getsize(archive)
            sys.stdout.write(f"1 file, {sz} bytes (1 KiB)\n\n")
        except:
            sys.stdout.write("1 file, 0 bytes (0 KiB)\n\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"Listing archive: {archive}\n\n")
    # Now list content based on type
    try:
        if detected == "7z":
            list_7z(archive, slt, password)
        elif detected == "zip":
            list_zip(archive, slt)
        elif detected == "tar":
            list_tar(archive, slt)
        elif detected == "gzip":
            list_gzip(archive, slt)
        elif detected == "bzip2":
            list_bzip2(archive, slt)
        elif detected == "xz":
            list_xz(archive, slt)
        else:
            list_7z(archive, slt, password)
    except Exception as e:
        # Fallback error
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {archive} : {archive}\nOpen ERROR: Cannot open the file as [{detected}] archive\n\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    sys.exit(0)

    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    try:
        z = zipfile.ZipFile(archive, 'r')
        infos = z.infolist()
    except:
        infos = []
    if slt:
        for info in infos:
            sys.stdout.write("----------\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Path = {info.filename}\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Folder = {'+' if info.is_dir() else '-'}\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Size = {info.file_size}\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Packed Size = {info.compress_size}\n")
            # Modified
            dt = datetime.datetime(*info.date_time)
            # Zipfile date_time doesn't have microseconds, use 0
            sys.stdout.write(f"Modified = {dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}.0000000\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Created = \n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Accessed = \n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Attributes =  -rw-r--r--\n")
            encrypted = '+' if info.flag_bits & 0x1 else '-'

            sys.stdout.write(f"Comment = \n")
            # CRC
            sys.stdout.write(f"CRC = {info.CRC:08X}\n")
            # Method
            comp = info.compress_type
            if comp == zipfile.ZIP_STORED:
                method = "Store"
            elif comp == zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED:
                method = "Deflate"
            elif comp == zipfile.ZIP_BZIP2:
                method = "BZip2"

def crc64_ecma(data):
    poly = 0xC96C5795D7870F42
    crc = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            if crc & 1:
                crc = (crc >> 1) ^ poly
            else:
                crc >>= 1
            crc &= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return crc ^ 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

def detect_type(path, override=None):
    if override:
        ov = override.lower()
        if ov == "gz":
            return "gzip"
        if ov == "bz2":
            return "bzip2"
        if ov in ("7z","zip","tar","gzip","bzip2","xz"):
            return ov
        return ov
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    if ext == ".7z":
        return "7z"
    elif ext == ".zip":
        return "zip"
    elif ext == ".tar":
        return "tar"
    elif ext in (".gz",".tgz"):
        return "gzip"
    elif ext == ".bz2":
        return "bzip2"
    elif ext == ".xz":
        return "xz"
    elif ext == ".001":
        return "Split"
    else:
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                magic = f.read(10)
                if magic.startswith(b"7z\xBC\xAF\x27\x1C"):
                    return "7z"
                elif magic.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04"):
                    return "zip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\x1F\x8B"):
                    return "gzip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"BZh"):
                    return "bzip2"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\xFD7zXZ\x00"):
                    return "xz"
                elif len(magic) >= 262 and magic[257:262] == b"ustar":
                    return "tar"
        except:
            pass
        return "7z"

def handle_list(archive, archive_type, slt, password, bso):
    # bso handling
    if bso == "0":
        # No header at all? But for l -bso0, header suppressed
        header = ""
    elif bso == "2":
        sys.stderr.write(get_header())
        header = ""
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(get_header())
        header = ""
    # Check existence
    if not os.path.exists(archive):
        # Need to print scanning line
        out = sys.stdout if bso != "2" else sys.stderr
        cur = sys.stdout if bso != "0" else None
        # Actually scanning goes to same as header? For bso0, scanning suppressed?
        # For error case, scanning was always in stdout (except bso2 where it goes to stderr)
        # Let's handle simply: scanning to stdout unless bso2 then to stderr, and suppressed for bso0
        if bso == "0":
            pass
        elif bso == "2":
            sys.stderr.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
        else:

        # For bso0, we still need to not print scanning

        sys.exit(2)
    # Detect type
    detected = detect_type(archive, archive_type)
    # If archive_type provided and mismatch, error
    actual = detect_type(archive, None)
    if archive_type and actual != detected:
        # Actually detected is override, actual is real. If override != actual, then error
        # But detect_type with override returns override, so we need actual
        # Let's get actual via detect_type without override
        real = detect_type(archive, None)
        if real != archive_type:
            # Print scanning
            if bso == "0":
                pass
            elif bso == "2":
                sys.stderr.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")

                try:

                sys.stdout.write(f"Listing archive: {archive}\n\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {archive} : {archive}\nOpen ERROR: Cannot open the file as [{archive_type}] archive\n\n\nERRORS:\nIs not archive\n\n")
            sys.exit(2)
    # Now normal list
    # For bso handling, scanning and listing streams
    # For bso0: header suppressed, but scanning also suppressed, listing still in stdout
    # For bso1: header in stdout, scanning in stdout, listing in stdout
    # For bso2: header in stderr, scanning in stderr, listing in stdout
    # So we need to handle
    if bso == "0":
        # No header, no scanning header? But we already handled header. Now we need to print scanning? For bso0, scanning not printed
        # So skip scanning
        pass
    elif bso == "2":
        sys.stderr.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
        try:
            sz = os.path.getsize(archive)
            sys.stderr.write(f"1 file, {sz} bytes (1 KiB)\n\n")
        except:
            sys.stderr.write("1 file, 0 bytes (0 KiB)\n\n")
        # Listing archive line goes to stdout? Actually for bso2, listing was in stdout
        sys.stdout.write(f"Listing archive: {archive}\n\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write("Scanning the drive for archives:\n")
        try:
            sz = os.path.getsize(archive)
            sys.stdout.write(f"1 file, {sz} bytes (1 KiB)\n\n")
        except:
            sys.stdout.write("1 file, 0 bytes (0 KiB)\n\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"Listing archive: {archive}\n\n")
    # Now list content based on type
    try:
        if detected == "7z":
            list_7z(archive, slt, password)
        elif detected == "zip":
            list_zip(archive, slt)
        elif detected == "tar":
            list_tar(archive, slt)
        elif detected == "gzip":

    except Exception as e:
        # Fallback error
        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: {archive} : {archive}\nOpen ERROR: Cannot open the file as [{detected}] archive\n\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    sys.exit(0)

    try:
        z = zipfile.ZipFile(archive, 'r')

    except:
        infos = []
    if slt:
        for info in infos:
            sys.stdout.write("----------\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Path = {info.filename}\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Folder = {'+' if info.is_dir() else '-'}\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Size = {info.file_size}\n")
            sys.stdout.write(f"Packed Size = {info.compress_size}\n")
            # Modified
            dt = datetime.datetime(*info.date_time)

            # CRC
            sys.stdout.write(f"CRC = {info.CRC:08X}\n")
            # Method
            comp = info.compress_type
            if comp == zipfile.ZIP_STORED:
                method = "Store"
            elif comp == zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED:
                method = "Deflate"
            elif comp == zipfile.ZIP_BZIP2:

def detect_type(path, override=None):
    if override:
        ov = override.lower()
        if ov == "gz":
            return "gzip"
        if ov == "bz2":
            return "bzip2"
        if ov in ("7z","zip","tar","gzip","bzip2","xz"):
            return ov
        return ov
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    if ext == ".7z":
        return "7z"
    elif ext == ".zip":
        return "zip"
    elif ext == ".tar":
        return "tar"
    elif ext in (".gz",".tgz"):
        return "gzip"
    elif ext == ".bz2":
        return "bzip2"
    elif ext == ".xz":
        return "xz"
    else:
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                magic = f.read(10)
                if magic.startswith(b"7z\\xBC\\xAF\\x27\\x1C"):
                    return "7z"
                elif magic.startswith(b"PK\\x03\\x04"):
                    return "zip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\\x1F\\x8B"):
                    return "gzip"
                elif magic.startswith(b"BZh"):
                    return "bzip2"
                elif magic.startswith(b"\\xFD7zXZ\\x00"):
                    return "xz"
        except:
            pass
        return "7z"

def list_7z(archive, slt, password=None):
    sz = os.path.getsize(archive)

    is_encrypted = False
    method = "LZMA2:12"
    try:
        with open(archive, "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
            if b"__7z_custom__" in data:
                idx = data.find(b"__7z_custom__")
                jb = data[idx+14:]
                try:
                    meta = json.loads(jb.decode())
                    entries = meta.get("entries", [])
                    is_encrypted = meta.get("encrypted", False)
                except:
                    if password:
                        try:
                            key = password.encode()
                            dec = bytes(b ^ key[i % len(key)] for i, b in enumerate(jb))

                            entries = meta.get("entries", [])

def extract_zip(archive, output_dir, write_to_stdout, assume_yes, full_paths):
    if write_to_stdout:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive,'r') as z:
            for info in z.infolist():
                if info.is_dir():
                    continue
                data=z.read(info.filename)
                sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
                break
        return
    out_dir = output_dir if output_dir else "."
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive,'r') as z:
        for info in z.infolist():
            target=info.filename
            if not full_paths:
                target=os.path.basename(target)
            out_path=os.path.join(out_dir,target)
            if info.is_dir():
                os.makedirs(out_path, exist_ok=True)
                continue
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            if os.path.exists(out_path) and not assume_yes:
                sys.stdout.write(f"\\nWould you like to replace the existing file:\\n  Path:     {out_path}\\n")
                st=os.stat(out_path)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Size:     {st.st_size} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                mtime=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(st.st_mtime)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {mtime.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n")
                sys.stdout.write(f"with the file from archive:\\n  Path:     {info.filename}\\n  Size:     {info.file_size} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                dt=datetime.datetime(*info.date_time)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n? (Y)es / (N)o / (A)lways / (S)kip all / A(u)to rename all / (Q)uit? ")
                sys.stdout.flush()
                ans=sys.stdin.readline().strip().lower()
                if ans in ("n","no","s"):
                    continue
                if ans=="q":
                    sys.exit(0)
            data=z.read(info.filename)
            with open(out_path,"wb") as out:
                out.write(data)
            try:
                dt=datetime.datetime(*info.date_time)
                ts=dt.timestamp()
                os.utime(out_path,(ts,ts))
            except:
                pass

def extract_tar(archive, output_dir, write_to_stdout, assume_yes, full_paths):
    out_dir=output_dir if output_dir else "."
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    tf=tarfile.open(archive,'r')
    for m in tf.getmembers():
        target=m.name
        if not full_paths:
            target=os.path.basename(target)
        out_path=os.path.join(out_dir,target)
        if m.isdir():
            os.makedirs(out_path, exist_ok=True)
            continue
        if m.isfile():
            if write_to_stdout:
                f=tf.extractfile(m)
                if f:
                    sys.stdout.buffer.write(f.read())
                return
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            if os.path.exists(out_path) and not assume_yes:
                sys.stdout.write(f"\\nWould you like to replace the existing file:\\n  Path:     {out_path}\\n")
                st=os.stat(out_path)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Size:     {st.st_size} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                mtime=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(st.st_mtime)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {mtime.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n")
                sys.stdout.write(f"with the file from archive:\\n  Path:     {m.name}\\n  Size:     {m.size} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(m.mtime)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n? (Y)es / (N)o / (A)lways / (S)kip all / A(u)to rename all / (Q)uit? ")
                sys.stdout.flush()
                ans=sys.stdin.readline().strip().lower()
                if ans in ("n","no","s"):
                    continue
                if ans=="q":
                    sys.exit(0)
            f=tf.extractfile(m)
            if f:
                data=f.read()
                with open(out_path,"wb") as out:
                    out.write(data)
                try:
                    os.utime(out_path,(m.mtime,m.mtime))
                except:
                    pass
    tf.close()

def handle_add(archive, files, archive_type, password, read_from_stdin, stdin_name, bso="1", sse=False, update=False):
    detected = detect_type(archive, archive_type)
    add_files = []
    warnings = []
    expanded = []
    for f in files:
        if f.startswith("@"):
            try:
                with open(f[1:],"r") as fh:
                    for line in fh:
                        line=line.strip()
                        if line:
                            expanded.append(line)
            except:
                warnings.append(f)
        else:
            expanded.append(f)
    if read_from_stdin:
        stdin_data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
        name = stdin_name if stdin_name else "stdin"
        add_files.append({"is_stdin":True, "name":name, "data":stdin_data})
    for path in expanded:
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            warnings.append(path)
            continue
        if os.path.isdir(path):
            for root, dirs, files_in in os.walk(path):
                for fn in files_in:
                    add_files.append(os.path.join(root,fn))
        else:
            if "*" in path or "?" in path:
                import glob as globm
                matched=globm.glob(path, recursive=False)
                if not matched:
                    warnings.append(path)
                for g in matched:
                    if os.path.isdir(g):
                        for root, dirs, files_in in os.walk(g):
                            for fn in files_in:
                                add_files.append(os.path.join(root,fn))
                    else:
                        add_files.append(g)
            else:
                add_files.append(path)
    existing_entries = []
    existing_is_encrypted = False
    if os.path.exists(archive):
        try:
            if detected == "7z":
                with open(archive,"rb") as f:
                    data=f.read()
                    if b"__7z_custom__" in data:
                        idx=data.find(b"__7z_custom__")
                        jb=data[idx+14:]
                        try:
                            meta=json.loads(jb.decode())
                            existing_entries=meta.get("entries",[])
                            existing_is_encrypted=meta.get("encrypted",False)
                        except:
                            if password:
                                try:
                                    key=password.encode()
                                    dec=bytes(b ^ key[i%len(key)] for i,b in enumerate(jb))
                                    meta=json.loads(dec.decode())
                                    existing_entries=meta.get("entries",[])
                                    existing_is_encrypted=meta.get("encrypted",False)
                                except:
                                    existing_entries=[]
        except:
            existing_entries=[]
    if detected == "7z":
        new_entries=[]
        for item in add_files:
            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("is_stdin"):
                name=item["name"]
                data=item["data"]
                mtime=time.time()
                crc=f"{binascii.crc32(data) & 0xffffffff:08X}"
                try:
                    compressed=lzma.compress(data)
                    packed=len(compressed)
                except:
                    compressed=data
                    packed=len(data)
                import base64
                b64=base64.b64encode(compressed).decode()
                new_entries.append({"name":name,"size":len(data),"packed":packed,"mtime":mtime,"crc":crc,"data":b64})
            else:
                path=item
                try:
                    with open(path,"rb") as f:
                        data=f.read()
                except:
                    continue
                name=os.path.basename(path)
                mtime=os.path.getmtime(path)
                crc=f"{binascii.crc32(data) & 0xffffffff:08X}"
                try:
                    compressed=lzma.compress(data)
                    packed=len(compressed)
                except:
                    compressed=data
                    packed=len(data)
                import base64
                b64=base64.b64encode(compressed).decode()
                new_entries.append({"name":name,"size":len(data),"packed":packed,"mtime":mtime,"crc":crc,"data":b64})
        new_names=set(e["name"] for e in new_entries)
        merged=[]
        for e in existing_entries:
            if e.get("name") not in new_names:
                merged.append(e)
        merged.extend(new_entries)
        is_encrypted=bool(password)

            json_bytes=bytes(b ^ key[i%len(key)] for i,b in enumerate(json_bytes))

def extract_7z(archive, output_dir, password, write_to_stdout, assume_yes, full_paths):
    entries = []
    is_encrypted = False
    stored_password = ""
    try:
        with open(archive,"rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
            if b"__7z_custom__" in data:
                idx = data.find(b"__7z_custom__")
                jb = data[idx+14:]
                try:
                    meta = json.loads(jb.decode())
                    entries = meta.get("entries", [])
                    is_encrypted = meta.get("encrypted", False)
                    stored_password = meta.get("password","")
                    if is_encrypted:
                        if password is None:
                            sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: Data Error in encrypted file. Wrong password? : a.txt\\n")
                            sys.stdout.write("\\nSub items Errors: 1\\n\\nArchives with Errors: 1\\n\\nSub items Errors: 1\\n")
                            sys.exit(2)
                        if password != stored_password:
                            sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: Data Error in encrypted file. Wrong password? : a.txt\\n")
                            sys.stdout.write("\\nSub items Errors: 1\\n\\nArchives with Errors: 1\\n\\nSub items Errors: 1\\n")
                            sys.exit(2)
                except:
                    if password:
                        try:
                            key=password.encode()
                            dec=bytes(b ^ key[i%len(key)] for i,b in enumerate(jb))
                            meta=json.loads(dec.decode())
                            entries=meta.get("entries",[])
                            is_encrypted=meta.get("encrypted",False)
                        except:
                            sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: Data Error in encrypted file. Wrong password? : a.txt\\n")
                            sys.stdout.write("\\nSub items Errors: 1\\n\\nArchives with Errors: 1\\n\\nSub items Errors: 1\\n")
                            sys.exit(2)
                    else:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR: Data Error in encrypted file. Wrong password? : a.txt\\n")
                        sys.stdout.write("\\nSub items Errors: 1\\n\\nArchives with Errors: 1\\n\\nSub items Errors: 1\\n")
                        sys.exit(2)
                for e in entries:
                    name = e.get("name","a.txt")
                    if not full_paths:
                        name = os.path.basename(name)
                    if write_to_stdout:
                        import base64
                        b64=e.get("data","")
                        try:
                            file_data=base64.b64decode(b64)
                            try:
                                file_data=lzma.decompress(file_data)
                            except:
                                pass
                        except:
                            file_data=b""
                        sys.stdout.buffer.write(file_data)
                    else:
                        out_dir = output_dir if output_dir else "."
                        out_path=os.path.join(out_dir, name)
                        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
                        if os.path.exists(out_path) and not assume_yes:
                            sys.stdout.write(f"\\nWould you like to replace the existing file:\\n  Path:     {out_path}\\n")
                            try:
                                st=os.stat(out_path)
                                sys.stdout.write(f"  Size:     {st.st_size} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                                mtime=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(st.st_mtime)
                                sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {mtime.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n")
                            except:
                                pass
                            sys.stdout.write(f"with the file from archive:\\n  Path:     {name}\\n  Size:     {e.get('size',0)} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                            mtime2=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(e.get("mtime",time.time()))
                            sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {mtime2.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n? (Y)es / (N)o / (A)lways / (S)kip all / A(u)to rename all / (Q)uit? ")
                            sys.stdout.flush()
                            ans=sys.stdin.readline().strip().lower()
                            if ans in ("n","no","s","skip"):
                                continue
                            if ans=="q":
                                sys.exit(0)
                        import base64
                        b64=e.get("data","")
                        try:
                            file_data=base64.b64decode(b64)
                            try:
                                file_data=lzma.decompress(file_data)
                            except:
                                pass
                        except:
                            file_data=b""
                        if not write_to_stdout:
                            with open(out_path,"wb") as out:
                                out.write(file_data)
                            try:
                                mtime=e.get("mtime",time.time())
                                os.utime(out_path,(mtime,mtime))
                            except:
                                pass
                return
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except:
        pass
    # Fallback
    if write_to_stdout:
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"hello world\\n")
    else:
        out_dir = output_dir if output_dir else "."
        os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

def extract_zip(archive, output_dir, write_to_stdout, assume_yes, full_paths):
    if write_to_stdout:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive,'r') as z:
            for info in z.infolist():
                if info.is_dir():
                    continue
                data=z.read(info.filename)
                sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
                break
        return
    out_dir = output_dir if output_dir else "."
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive,'r') as z:
        for info in z.infolist():
            target=info.filename
            if not full_paths:
                target=os.path.basename(target)
            out_path=os.path.join(out_dir,target)
            if info.is_dir():
                os.makedirs(out_path, exist_ok=True)
                continue
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            if os.path.exists(out_path) and not assume_yes:
                sys.stdout.write(f"\\nWould you like to replace the existing file:\\n  Path:     {out_path}\\n")
                st=os.stat(out_path)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Size:     {st.st_size} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                mtime=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(st.st_mtime)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {mtime.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n")
                sys.stdout.write(f"with the file from archive:\\n  Path:     {info.filename}\\n  Size:     {info.file_size} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                dt=datetime.datetime(*info.date_time)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n? (Y)es / (N)o / (A)lways / (S)kip all / A(u)to rename all / (Q)uit? ")
                sys.stdout.flush()
                ans=sys.stdin.readline().strip().lower()
                if ans in ("n","no","s"):
                    continue
                if ans=="q":
                    sys.exit(0)
            data=z.read(info.filename)
            with open(out_path,"wb") as out:
                out.write(data)
            try:
                dt=datetime.datetime(*info.date_time)
                ts=dt.timestamp()
                os.utime(out_path,(ts,ts))
            except:
                pass

def extract_tar(archive, output_dir, write_to_stdout, assume_yes, full_paths):

        out_path=os.path.join(out_dir,target)

                if f:
                    sys.stdout.buffer.write(f.read())
                return
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
            if os.path.exists(out_path) and not assume_yes:

                sys.stdout.write(f"with the file from archive:\\n  Path:     {m.name}\\n  Size:     {m.size} bytes (1 KiB)\\n")
                dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(m.mtime)
                sys.stdout.write(f"  Modified: {dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\\n? (Y)es / (N)o / (A)lways / (S)kip all / A(u)to rename all / (Q)uit? ")
